<system-reminder>
# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## bioRxiv
An MCP server for accessing bioRxiv and medRxiv preprint servers.

This server provides:
- Tools: Search preprints, get preprint details, list subject categories
- Prompts: Analyze preprint methodology and findings

bioRxiv is a preprint server for biological sciences operated by Cold Spring
Harbor Laboratory. It hosts research manuscripts that have NOT undergone peer
review. This server wraps the official bioRxiv API to provide structured access
to preprint metadata, abstracts, and full-text PDFs.

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:
• search_preprints: Find preprints by date range and/or subject category (no keyword, author, or full-text search) - primary discovery tool
• get_preprint: Get full details for a specific preprint by DOI
• get_categories: List available subject categories for filtering
• search_published_preprints: Find preprints that have been formally published in journals
• funder_search: Find preprints by funding source (NIH, etc.)
• get_statistics: Usage and submission statistics

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive literature analysis:
1. Use search_preprints to find relevant preprints by date range and category
2. Use get_preprint for detailed information on promising results
3. Use search_published_preprints to check if preprints have been peer-reviewed and published
4. Use funder_search to identify research funding patterns in a field

For tracking research trends:
1. Use get_categories to identify relevant subject areas
2. Use search_preprints with date filters for recent activity
3. Use get_statistics to understand submission volumes


## Claude_Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## Consensus
Consensus is a research paper search engine: relevance-ranked semantic search over 400M+ peer-reviewed papers (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, PubMed). Use the `search` tool to look up papers for a scientific query; it takes plain-language queries and returns ranked paper records. When presenting search results, you MUST cite papers inline using their numbered references from the tool result (e.g. [1], [2], [3]). When discussing findings, always attribute them to specific papers: 'Caffeine improves endurance performance [1] and reduces perceived exertion [3].' At the end of your response, list all cited papers as numbered references with their titles hyperlinked to the URLs from the tool result: [1] [Paper Title](url) (Authors, Year, Journal, Citations). Use the exact paper URLs from the tool result — do not modify, shorten, or regenerate them. Do not omit paper links or summarize results without citing specific papers. IMPORTANT: Some search results end with a sign-up, upgrade, or usage message. When a result has one, you MUST include it at the END of your response word-for-word: do not omit, shorten, or rephrase it. When a result has none, do not add one: never write your own upgrade prompt, search count, or Consensus link. Batch at most 3 search calls at a time to avoid rate limits. For a broad request (a review, screening, finding everything on a topic), make one search with a large page_size rather than many narrower searches. If you receive a rate limit error, wait 30 seconds before retrying. Do NOT apply search filters (year_min, year_max, study_types, domain, human, sample_size_min, sjr_max, controlled, sjr_min, citation_min, open_access, country) unless the user explicitly requests them or clearly expresses intent to narrow results. If the user asks a research question without mentioning filtering criteria, call search with only the query parameter.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

1	# The lens of a code value: the recording session judges and writes it; the maps only propose (revised design)
2	
3	**Status.** Written 2026-11-15 by an Opus-class designer on the owner's instruction ("have Opus design mapping for codes and identities etc then fold into remediation plan and finalize it"), then revised after an independent critic's attack (findings: `scratchpad/session_2026-11-13-edmonton-checklist-pass/sweep/adj/CRITIC-MAPPING.md`). The first version (a read-time crossing view and an engine edit) was withdrawn. Not read by the owner. The ledger outranks this document (CLAUDE.md rule 0); the term-resolution plan outranks the remediation plan where they conflict. Counts come from commands given beside them: re-run, do not trust. The designer edited no repository file; the end-to-end run used scratch copies of the database, and the repository database's sha256 (`3c575c89…`) was unchanged.
4	
5	**What changed from the first version.** The read-time crossing (`v_figure_identity`, an edit to `_lens_clause`) and the claim that OR-1 is superseded are dropped. The recording session judges a code value's lens and writes it, identity included. The maps become the writer's source of proposals. Two of the three proposed tasks dissolve; two of the three owner questions are withdrawn.
6	
7	## 1. The crossing
8	
9	**What each map holds (re-verified):**
10	- `identity_icf_map`: identity → ICF, many-to-many, 61 rows, each with mechanism, `mapping_confidence` and provenance.
11	- `access_need_icf`: need → ICF, 43 rows, no provenance column and no `db.py` writer; 38 rows are e-codes; five are b/d codes: A-PRECISION b765, A-TIME b164, A-SELFCARE d510/d540/d550 (`select need_code, icf_code from access_need_icf where icf_type<>'e'`).
12	- The medical maps hold 0 rows.
13	- No live table maps needs to identities. Migration 109 dropped the earlier route: `population_axis_map` (53 rows) and `access_need_axis_map` (21 rows) (`scripts/migrations/109_drop_axes.sql:6-12,44-45`).
14	
15	**Where the crossing happens: at recording, by judgment.** The owner's words: "all code values will have a lens even if it's not explicitly stated. use contextual judgment"; "at the moment of recording the row is when you will have best idea of context"; "typically anything to do concerning mounting height will concern wheelchair users"; "yes lens in judgment"; "ICF and access needs are supposed to be mapped to populations too so populations still get coded as a result". Rule 8: the script asks for a judgment and records it with its warrant. In the call that records a code value, the session writes: the ICF link, the access-need link, and an **identity link for each group it judges the value serves**; each link with `basis` `context`, `basis_text` (the source's words) and `basis_reason` (the judgment): T-126's two cells.
16	
17	**The writer is legal today.** `extraction_lens_links` allows one lens per row and several rows per figure. Extractions 33 (`A-EFFORT, MOB`) and 165 (`A-EFFORT, MS`) already carry an identity row beside a need row. (The first version's claim that writing the identity would break the CHECK was false.)
18	
19	**Rule 5 is not breached.** A map row says a group typically has a limitation in an activity. A link says this clause serves that group, on its own warrant. They are different facts. D-0182 answered the 2026-08-28 "copy of the map" argument by ruling multiplicity acceptable (ledger line 2572).
20	
21	**The engine does not change.** `_lens_clause` stays as D-0184 and OR-1 ruled: a figure reaches a cell only through the links written on it (`scripts/assess/assess_cell.py:242-257`). OR-1 is not superseded; there is no view.
22	
23	**Two ledger corrections must be appended on contact (rule 0), in the plan-fold commit** (a ledger entry needs no attestation):
24	- (i) The sixteenth-set entry's ACTION "reach the populations through the mapping; do not store the derived identity beside them" was the recorder's reading under an [ASSUMPTION], not the owner's words. Replace it: populations are coded "as a result" of the ICF and need links because the maps propose and the session confirms and writes them.
25	- (ii) OD-31's option text, "under a general disability heading, no identity, only its ICF and access-need lenses", is superseded for code values whose context the session judges; it still holds for the `heading` basis. Prose supersession only (the ledger cannot carry a marker beside its own earlier text).
26	
27	## 2. The proposals and the missing rows
28	
29	**(a) Need → identity proposals: read nothing new.**
30	
31	| Option | Verdict | Why |
32	|---|---|---|
33	| Rebuild the dropped axis maps | Rejected | "Axes" is retired vocabulary the owner told us not to relitigate; WRK-181 asks for population ↔ ICF pairs, which is `identity_icf_map`'s job, not a need route |
34	| Add need → b/d rows to `access_need_icf` | Rejected for now | Needs a provenance column and a new writer; the proposals they would add are reachable more directly from the figure's own ICF link |
35	| New `identity_need_map` | Rejected | A second home beside `access_needs.absorbs`, and code that adds no proposal a judging session needs |
36	| Propose from what exists | **Chosen** | No new table, column or verb |
37	
38	How it works: the writer proposes identities from `identity_icf_map` for the ICF codes the session is about to write, plus `access_need_icf`'s existing b/d rows for its needs. Each proposal shows its `mapping_confidence`, mechanism and provenance. It also shows the need's own registry text (`design_obligation`, `absorbs`) as reading for the judge, never parsed. OR-1 requires every relevant model on a figure, so a code value carries an ICF code and the ICF side always yields proposals. Proposals are aids, not a whitelist: the session may write any live identity, with its warrant. `access_needs.absorbs` stays (`joined_cells_census.py` flags it, 16 of 17 rows delimited); with no need → identity table beside it there is no second home; splitting it is a schema-shape gap to be filed, not part of this design.
39	
40	**(b) The ICF code for reach.** ICF nests d4452 *Reaching* under d445 *Hand and arm use* (siblings: pulling, pushing, turning, throwing, catching); d4153 *Maintaining a sitting position* and d4154 *Maintaining a standing position* nest under d415. These titles are from the designer's knowledge and unverified: the research task fetches the WHO payload. The d-chapter records activity limitations: wheelchair users are limited in reaching, from a seated reach range, but not in hand and arm use as a whole, so the child is the true claim and the parent over-claims. `base_icf` has no hierarchy and `_lens_clause` matches codes exactly, so a d4452 figure does not reach a d445 cell. **Writer rule:** propose the most specific code the clause supports, and show the parent beside it. **Codes to mint** (`db.py add-icf-code --title-payload <WHO payload>`): d4452, d4153, d4154; title d415. Then map WHEEL → d4452 and WHEEL → d4154 or d4153 (the batch judges which), with mechanism and provenance. **Five identities with no ICF row** (ADHD, DEAFBLIND, EPI, MS, VES) get proposed rows re-derived from `population_axis_map` and each axis's ICF anchors (`governance/functional-taxonomy.md:150-154`): WRK-181's direction, which migration 109 calls "an owner item". **BAR, LPA, TALL get no anchor** (the 2026-09-11 ruling cited in migration 109): judged directly, never proposed.
41	
42	**Who judges.** The batch session judges each row. The owner confirms the full list in one answer (OD-67) before the data pull request merges, because these rows decide which people a value serves: population taxonomy.
43	
44	**(c) The marker.** The ledger's ACTION on thin: "derive thin from the population match and the proxy-inference record; do not count roots to decide it; do not store it beside them" (ledger 7089-7096). A `context` link is neither of those records, and `context` is refused below tier 4 (T-126). So: a code value carries its regulatory stratum's marker, which `specifications`' CHECK forces to ○ when `regulatory_stratum_only`; a context link adds no ⚠. A research figure's identity comes only from its own words or its study's participants, so thin stays derived from PROXY grades, as ruled. The mounting-height default shows its marker plus the visible label "assigned: mounting height; typically concerns wheelchair users" (basis `context`): the owner's rule of thumb, recorded with its warrant, not the project's conjecture about evidence. The earlier OD-69 (research figures naming no group) is withdrawn: the `context` basis cannot reach research figures.
45	
46	**(d) End to end on a scratch copy.** T-102's WHEEL simulated as a child of MOB; d4452 minted with WHEEL → d4452; a scratch parameter "control mounting height"; a T6 code row "Controls shall be mounted at a height of not more than 1200 mm" recorded with three links: d4452, A-REACH and WHEEL (`basis='heading'` stood in for `context`, which today's CHECK does not admit). `determine` gave: WHEEL; WHEEL+d4452; WHEEL+A-REACH; d4452; A-REACH: in lens, `n_sources` 1, state `pending`, `regulatory_stratum_only` 1, `gap_needed` True; MOB: refused (no figure; T-055's parent gather is not built); BLIND: refused, correctly. So the owner's default reaches the WHEEL cell with no engine change; it reads `pending` because one T6 source fails the §2.3 richness rule, the expected state for a code-only cell. MOB is reached once T-055 lands.
47	
48	## 3. The engine
49	
50	No change, and no supersession of D-0184 or OR-1. The scratch run reaches the WHEEL cell through the written link; per-figure `EXISTS` (251-253) and `SELECT DISTINCT e.ref_id` (274) already stop a figure with links in two lens columns being counted twice; `link_payload`, `RULE_VERSION`, K01 and the six `_lens_clause` callers are untouched; the skill prose at `skills/run-pipeline_SKILL.md:261` ("only through the live lens links written on it") stays true.
51	
52	## 4. Coverage and guards
53	
54	- **Writer (T-126):** `add-extraction` and `add-lens-link` print the proposals before writing and return `identities_proposed` and `identities_written`. A tier-4-or-above row written with ICF or need links but no identity link, while the maps propose one, prints `WARNING: maps propose <codes> (confidence, provenance); no identity written`. It flags rather than refuses.
55	- **Audit:** one audit, registered **advisory** in `governance/check-registry.yaml`, printing `EXAMINED: n`; it lists by id every live figure with ICF or need links and no identity link, and every identity the maps never propose. The contract gains one judgment-stage criterion pointing at it (precedent `base-medical-lens-offered-not-adopted`, `governance/pipeline-contract.yaml:35-45`). There are 145 live tier-4-or-above links today (derive by command); all 216 links are `carried`.
56	- **Flip to blocking: T-059's tooling pull request**, after T-127 and T-128. T-059's selection depends on every code value carrying a lens, and rule 10 bars the research batches from editing the registry.
57	- **Reader minimum:** every link renders with its basis, so a context-assigned group shows as assigned. Figures the audit lists render under "no group judged yet". Nothing is dropped.
58	
59	## 5. Tasks
60	
61	- **T-126 (tooling, wave 1)** carries: the `context` basis and `basis_reason` column (unchanged); **reversed:** §4 item 4 now writes the judged identity link, which "No identity link is written" forbade; the proposal display and warning; the advisory audit and criterion; the ICF registry command extended to `'%reaching%'` so it prints d4452 once minted (as written, its `'%hand and arm%'` prints d445); the skill paragraph (the defaults, proposals as aids, writing the identity). §8's "do not add map rows" stays, pointing at T-128. Still no engine change.
62	- **T-127 (research)** carries the judged ICF, need and identity links for stored code rows, chosen from the proposals; it runs **after T-102 and T-128**, so rows are tagged WHEEL and d4452 once, not MOB and d445 and then swept again [ASSUMPTION: T-102 step 4 already carries MOB rows by judgment; the ledger warns against sweeping the same rows twice].
63	- **The new-table task and the engine task dissolve.** The map-filling batch survives as **T-128 (RESEARCH)** (next free number: `ls tasks | grep -oE '^T-[0-9]+' | sort -u | tail -3` prints T-127): mints d4452, d4153, d4154 and titles d415 from WHO payloads, writes WHEEL → reach and seated rows, writes the five WRK-181 rows; every row through `add-icf-code` and `add-population-icf-link` with mechanism, confidence and provenance, after OD-67's confirmation; depends on T-102 (WHEEL minted, SCI retired, which needs T-054 and T-055); needs no new tooling.
64	- **T-059:** adds T-128 as a precondition and flips the audit to blocking. **T-110:** adds T-128. **T-115:** unchanged (under OD-31 its `ALL` retags get ICF and need links plus judged identities through T-126's writer). **T-018, T-019, T-055, T-091, T-102:** unchanged.
65	- **Pull request order:** T-126 → (T-054, T-055, T-102 as already planned) → T-128 → T-127 → T-115 → T-059 → T-110.
66	- **Open items:** OI-73 is resolved by T-126's proposals plus T-128; OI-74 closes with no traversal: the identity is written.
67	
68	**Tests:**
69	
70	| Test | Defect it catches | Red before T-126? |
71	|---|---|---|
72	| T126-01 (revised) | Mounting-height row: links d4452, A-REACH, WHEEL by `context`; the WHEEL cell gathers it; the result lists the WHEEL proposal from the map with its confidence and provenance. Catches a writer that hides proposals or refuses the identity | Yes |
73	| T126-11 | ICF-only code row whose map proposes an identity: the warning prints and the audit lists the row. Catches a silent omission | Yes |
74	| T126-12 | The audit omits a figure that has an identity link and reports `EXAMINED > 0`. Catches a vacuous audit | Yes (no audit exists) |
75	| T128-A (live after-test) | A WHEEL → d4452 row exists and the scratch run returns WHEEL in lens. Catches a map gap | Red until T-128 |
76	
77	Dropped as unable to go red: the first version's X-04, X-05, X-07 and the parity check.
78	
79	## 6. Owner question
80	
81	- **OD-67. May the batch's full list of new population-to-ICF rows be confirmed in one answer?** The list: wheelchair users → reaching and seated or standing posture, and the five groups with no row (ADHD, DeafBlind, epilepsy, MS, vestibular) re-derived from the retired axis map. Recommended: **yes, in one answer, as for the mobility crossings (OI-03)**: these rows decide which groups are proposed for every code value, which is population taxonomy and the owner's.
82	
83	## 7. Risks and what the designer could not check
84	
85	**Risks.** A proposal anchors judgment: a recorder may accept whatever the map proposes (figure 166, one d450 link, would propose BRAIN, COM, MOB, PAIN and SCI); the guard is the visible mechanism and confidence plus the warrant the session must state. Until T-102, the default writes MOB, not WHEEL. A d4452 cell and a d445 cell never meet, because there is no ICF hierarchy.
86	
87	**Not checked.** The WHO titles; which SCI rows T-102 carries; the 2026-09-11 "no anchor" ruling text; rulings in `sessions/`.
88	
89	## Disposition of the critic's points
90	
91	| # | Point | Disposition |
92	|---|---|---|
93	| 1 | Intersection hides groups | Fixed: no read-time rule; proposals are not a whitelist (ten identities have no map row, verified) |
94	| 2 | The first OD-67's benefit false | Accepted; withdrawn; the number reused for the map-row confirmation |
95	| 3 | Inflation in the adopted direction | Accepted (figure 166 verified); fixed: the map only proposes |
96	| 4 | Read time was the designer's reading; the CHECK claim false | Accepted (extractions 33 and 165 verified) |
97	| 5 | Prior homes omitted | Accepted; weighed in 2(a); D-0169 says `access_need_icf` "maps needs to ICF e-codes", so e was the design, not a ban |
98	| 6 | `link_payload` and `RULE_VERSION` | Moot: no engine change |
99	| 7 | Unlisted readers | Moot for the engine; the prose stays true |
100	| 8 | Tests that cannot go red | Accepted; dropped |
101	| 9 | Blocking unassigned, PR order, deferred supersession, T-126 command | Fixed: T-059 flips the audit; the order lists T-054, T-055, T-102 (T-019 is merged); the ledger corrections go in on contact; T-126's command is extended |
102	| 10 | d4452 is a child of d445 | Answered in 2(b) |
103	| 11 | Thin marker inconsistent | Fixed in 2(c) |

23-
24-## 2. sr_meta placement — T2, not T3
25-
26-The decision: systematic reviews and meta-analyses sit at **Tier 2** alongside named-organisation evidence-based standards.
27-
28-The reasoning, in declining priority:
29-
30:1. **PI v10.14 line 138 reading.** Rule #9 step 5 enumerates "Tier 1 / Co-1 / Tier 2 / Co-2 / Tier 3 evidence" with T4 / T5 explicitly excluded ("Tier 4 international / Tier 5 national-recommended excluded at this step"). The natural reading positions T2 as the synthesis-tier above T3 primary clinical work and below international standards. SR / meta-analysis is the canonical example of synthesis above primary studies.
31-2. **Evidence-type homology.** T2's other occupants (`standard_eb` from named DPOs / professional bodies) are themselves synthesis-tier — they aggregate primary evidence into a consensus position. SR / meta-analysis aggregates primary evidence into a statistical consensus position. Same epistemic move, different machinery.
32-3. **Citation behaviour.** When a Guidebook claim cites both an SR and a primary clinical study, the SR is treated as the warrant-source and the primary study as one of the inputs the SR weighed. The warrant-source must rank above the input-source. SR > primary clinical.
33-4. **GRADE alignment.** The GRADE framework places systematic reviews / meta-analyses of RCTs at the top of the evidence-quality hierarchy. The Guidebook does not adopt GRADE wholesale (the Guidebook reads built-environment claims rather than treatment-effect claims), but the synthesis-above-primary principle is the same.
34-
35-The four sr_meta rows previously sitting at T3 are migrated to T2 by `scripts/migrations/data_20260525070000_sr_meta_t2_canonicalization.sql`.
36-
37-**Scoping reviews and conceptual/framework papers are T3, not T2 (DR-2026-07-21).** `sr_meta` (T2) is reserved for *systematic* reviews and meta-analyses — a defined method with risk-of-bias appraisal and/or effect synthesis. A **scoping review** maps a literature without appraisal (a weaker synthesis) and anchors at **T3**; a peer-reviewed **conceptual/framework paper** (e.g. a design-index proposal such as ASPECTSS) is primary work, also **T3**. Relatedly (DR-2026-07-21): **national accessibility standards** (DIN 18040, BS 8300) and **professional-body design guides** (e.g. the RIBA/Habinteg Inclusive Housing Design Guide) sit at **T5** `national_fw` at the standard/guidance level — a specific provision only becomes T6 when cited as a legally-enforceable adopted code floor (the T5-vs-T6 split already drawn in §1's table).
38-
39-## 3. Best-practice ≠ convergence
40-
41-A separate canonical clarification, surfaced 2026-05-25 during reverification scoping.
42-
43:**The convergence-not-evidence trap.** A claim of the form "BS 8300, DIN 18040-1, Part M, and AS 1428.1 all specify X" is a **convergence claim across Tier 4–6 sources**. Convergence is informative — it tells us multiple jurisdictions adopted the same value. Convergence is NOT best-practice evidence — the jurisdictions could all be wrong together, or could all be reading from a single shared earlier source that itself rests on no evidence, or could all reflect pre-evidence regulatory floors that no jurisdiction has updated.
44-
45-**The corridor-width worked example.** Multiple Tier 5/6 codes converge on 1800mm two-wheelchair-passing. Co-1/T2/T3 evidence (DSDG Bauman 2010, DeafScape Vaughn 2018, Cloete & Rout 2025) anchors 2440mm primary corridors. The 1800mm convergence describes the regulatory floor; the 2440mm Co-1/T2/T3 anchor describes best practice. Labelling 1800mm "preferred" or "best practice" because it converges across T5/T6 jurisdictions is the failure mode this section names.
46-
47:**The implication for citation tiering.** Tier 4–6 citations are valid for code-baseline claims (this is the legal floor in jurisdiction X) and for jurisdiction-tracking work.
48-
49:> **⚠ Superseded 2026-07-20 by §8.** The original text here read *"they do not — by themselves — anchor best-practice claims. Best-practice claims require T1, Co-1, T2, or Co-2 evidence."* That binary is replaced by the **weighted-strength anchor model** (§8): a T4–T6-only claim *may* be stated, but is rendered at partial/weak strength with an explicit honesty flag. The convergence-not-evidence principle above is retained as the honesty rule for the weak band.
50-
51:## 4. Code-currency check is part of citing T4–T6
52-
53:When a BPC cites a T4–T6 source, the citation must additionally confirm that the cited edition is the **current legally-in-force edition** — not a superseded edition. Pre-existing supersession_check rows surface this for the supersession protocol; the same check applies inline to any new T4–T6 citation.
54-
55-**Enforcement.** The currency fact is carried in the `evidence_sources.code_currency_*` columns; no mechanical check reads it since `scripts/audit/code_currency_audit.py` was deleted (plan step 1.6, RULINGS R4).
56-
57-`code_currency_status` enum: `VERIFIED-CURRENT`, `PERMANENT-FRAMEWORK` (foundational references like CRPD, ICF, WHO Child Growth Standards that do not revise on the same cadence), `SUPERSEDED-PENDING-REPLACEMENT`, `UNVERIFIED-CHECK-DEFERRED` (e.g., T6 codes flagged in MOB Pass-2 supersession audit as out-of-scope per DR-2026-05-24).
58-
59-Worked example surfaced 2026-05-25: `accessible-circulation-geometry.md` cites DIN 18040-1:2010-10. The 2010 edition is still legally in force in Germany (referenced in MVV TB 2024/1 published August 2024), but draft revision E DIN 18040-1:2023-02 exists and DIN EN 17210:2021 has been published as the European harmonised accessibility standard. A reverification of the BPC must consider whether the 2010 citation should be retained, supplemented, or replaced. Counter-example same day: NZS 4121:2001 is 24 years old but remains the NZ Building Act §119 / D1/AS1 Acceptable Solution per NZ Ministry of Education March 2025 guidance; age does NOT predict supersession.
60-
61-## 5. evidence_quality marker mapping
62-
63-`skills/guidebook-auditor_SKILL.md` §4.2 inline quality markers map to the canonical ladder:
64-- `●` confirmed evidence base: T1, T2 (sr_meta + standard_eb + co2), **T3 clinical** (lower-control primary clinical research — confirmed primary evidence, lower control level), Co-1, Co-2
65:- `◐` policy or standards basis only, not primary evidence: T4, T5
66-- `○` grey literature, expert consensus, thin base, unconfirmed: T3 grey, `[EXPERT CONSENSUS]`, `[THIN BASE]`, `[UNSUPPORTED]`, T6 (code-floor), a source that could not be retrieved and so stays `UNVERIFIED` (owner, 2026-10-21: it cannot be claimed as primary evidence or at a top tier)
67-
68-The T3 split is deliberate: T3 holds two species (per §1) — lower-control *primary clinical* research and *grey-literature* primary research. The clinical species is confirmed primary evidence (just lower control) and maps to `●`; the grey species maps to `○`. The earlier version of this map listed only "T3 grey → ○" and left T3-clinical unplaced (R9-c).

++ b/scripts/tests/test_db_amend_writers.py
    # ── T126: a code value's lens is judged from its context when its row is recorded; the maps propose ────────────
    # Every code is derived from the copy's registries; where one is not live yet (the Reaching code before T-128) the
    # fixture mints it on the COPY only, with one identity_icf_map row joining the wheelchair-user identity to it, and
    # says so, so the case keeps asserting the path once the live row exists. The clause and the source's scope clause
    # are saved as a real file for the fixture source (and another for a second source) in the fixture retrieval-log root.
    sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO / "scripts" / "assess"))
    import assess_cell as _t126_engine                                 # noqa: E402

    def t126_first(sql, *params):
        rows = q(sql, *params)
        return rows[0][0] if rows else None

    T126_CTX = ("--claim-type", "absent", "--figure-role", "finding", "--relation", "none",
                "--extraction-method", "skim", "--session", S)
    T126_REASON = "typically concerns wheelchair users"
    reach126 = t126_first("SELECT icf_code FROM base_icf WHERE lower(coalesce(title,'')) LIKE '%reaching%' ORDER BY icf_code")
    wheel126 = t126_first(
        "SELECT i.identity_code FROM base_taxonomy_identity i WHERE i.status='active' AND lower(i.display_name||' '||"
        "coalesce(i.description,'')) LIKE '%wheelchair%' ORDER BY (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM base_taxonomy_identity c "
        "WHERE c.parent_code = i.identity_code AND c.status='active'), i.parent_code IS NULL, i.identity_code")
    need126 = t126_first("SELECT need_code FROM access_needs WHERE lower(coalesce(design_obligation,'')) LIKE '%reachable%' "
                         "AND lower(design_obligation) LIKE '%seated%' ORDER BY need_code")
    clear126 = t126_first("SELECT icf_code FROM base_icf WHERE lower(coalesce(title,'')) LIKE '%moving around using equipment%'")
    blind126 = t126_first("SELECT identity_code FROM base_taxonomy_identity WHERE status='active' AND "
                          "lower(display_name) LIKE '%blind%' AND lower(display_name) LIKE '%low%vision%'")
    reach_fixture = reach126 is None
    if reach_fixture:
        reach126 = "d4452"
        w("INSERT INTO base_icf (icf_code, component, title, title_source, created_at, created_by_session) "
          "VALUES (?, 'd', 'Reaching', 'TASK-FIXTURE T126', 't', ?)", reach126, S)
    if wheel126 and not q("SELECT 1 FROM identity_icf_map WHERE identity_code=? AND icf_code=? AND retired_at IS NULL",
                          wheel126, reach126):
        w("INSERT INTO identity_icf_map (identity_code, icf_code, mechanism, mapping_confidence, provenance, created_at, "
          "created_by_session) VALUES (?, ?, 'TASK-FIXTURE seated reach', 'moderate_contextual', 'TASK-FIXTURE T126', "
          "'2026-01-01 00:00', ?)", wheel126, reach126, S)
    print(f"      T126 codes: reach {reach126} ({'fixture row' if reach_fixture else 'live'}), need {need126}, "
          f"identity {wheel126}, clearance {clear126}, override {blind126}")

    T126_CLAUSE = "TASK-FIXTURE T126 Controls shall be mounted at a height of not more than 1200 mm"
    T126_KNEE = "TASK-FIXTURE T126 Knee clearance under the counter shall be not less than 685 mm"
    T126_PROTRUDE = ("TASK-FIXTURE T126 Objects protruding more than 100 mm into the path shall be detectable by "
                     "people who are blind or have low vision")
    T126_SCOPE = "TASK-FIXTURE T126 This section applies to sanitary rooms in assembly occupancies"
    T126_OTHER = "TASK-FIXTURE T126 phrase saved only for another source"
    log_root = pathlib.Path(os.environ["GUIDEBOOK_RETRIEVAL_LOG"]) / "task-fixture-t126"
    log_root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    def t126_save(ref, name, body):
        (log_root / name).write_text(body, encoding="utf-8")
        with open(log_root / "manifest.jsonl", "a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            fh.write(json.dumps({"ref_id": ref, "artefact": name, "content_type": "text/plain",
                                 "url": f"https://example.org/task-fixture/{name}"}) + "\n")

    code126, _ = add_o("T126 code", "--evidence-type", "code")
    readable(code126)
    other126, _ = add_o("T126 other code", "--evidence-type", "code")
    readable(other126)
    grey126, _ = add_o("T126 research", "--evidence-type", "grey")
    readable(grey126)
    t126_save(code126, "t126-code.txt", "\n".join([T126_SCOPE, T126_CLAUSE, T126_KNEE, T126_PROTRUDE]))
    t126_save(other126, "t126-other.txt", T126_OTHER)
    t126_save(grey126, "t126-grey.txt", T126_CLAUSE)

    def t126_add(ref, clause, *lens, section="TASK-FIXTURE T126 Section 3.8"):
        r = run_cli("add-extraction", "--ref-id", ref, "--parameter-id", str(PARAM), *lens, "--claim-text", clause,
                    "--source-section", section, *T126_CTX)
        got = q("SELECT extraction_id FROM source_value_extractions WHERE ref_id=? AND claim_text=? "
                "ORDER BY extraction_id DESC", ref, clause)
        try:
            res = json.loads(r.stdout) if r.returncode == 0 else {}
        except ValueError:
            res = {}
        return r, (got[0][0] if got else None), res

    def t126_links(fig):
        return t018_read("SELECT identity_code, icf_code, needs_code, basis, basis_text, basis_reason FROM "
                         "v_live_lens_links WHERE extraction_id=? ORDER BY link_id", fig)

    CTX = lambda words: ("--lens-basis", "context", "--lens-basis-text", words, "--lens-basis-reason", T126_REASON)  # noqa: E731

    # T126-01: the owner's mounting-height default: three links by context, the proposal shown, the cell gathers it.
    r01_, fig126, res01 = t126_add(code126, T126_CLAUSE, "--icf", reach126, "--needs", need126, "--identity", wheel126,
                                   *CTX("mounted at a height"))
    links01, e01 = t126_links(fig126) if fig126 else (None, "no figure")
    gathered = None
    if fig126:
        _gc = sqlite3.connect(DB)
        try:
            gathered = [g for g in _t126_engine.gather_extraction_links(_gc, PARAM, [], {"identity_code": wheel126})
                        if g["extraction_id"] == fig126]
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 -- recorded red below
            gathered = f"{exc.__class__.__name__}: {exc}"
        finally:
            _gc.close()
    record("T126-01", "a mounting-height code row is recorded with the reach ICF code, the reach need and the wheelchair-user "
           "identity by context, the words and the reason in two cells; the map's proposal is printed and returned, "
           "and the identity cell gathers the figure",
           r01_.returncode == 0 and links01 is not None and len(links01) == 3
           and all(l[3:] == ("context", "mounted at a height", T126_REASON) for l in links01)
           and res01.get("identities_proposed") and wheel126 in res01["identities_proposed"]
           and res01.get("identities_written") == [wheel126]
           and f"{wheel126}: via ICF {reach126}" in r01_.stderr and "moderate_contextual" in r01_.stderr
           and "provenance" in r01_.stderr
           and isinstance(gathered, list) and len(gathered) == 1 and gathered[0]["in_lens"],
           f"rc={r01_.returncode} {out_of(r01_)[-300:]!r} links={links01} {e01} res={res01} gathered={gathered}")

    # T126-02: knee clearance, the second default; the live map proposes the wheelchair-user family for the clearance code.
    r02_, fig02_, res02 = t126_add(code126, T126_KNEE, "--icf", clear126, "--needs", need126, "--identity", wheel126,
                                   *CTX("knee clearance"))
    live_prop02 = [c for (c,) in q("SELECT DISTINCT identity_code FROM identity_icf_map WHERE icf_code=? AND retired_at "
                                   "IS NULL ORDER BY 1", clear126)]
    record("T126-02", "a knee-clearance code row is recorded with the clearance ICF code, the reach need and the wheelchair-user "
           "identity by context; the proposals are the live map's rows for the clearance code",
           r02_.returncode == 0 and fig02_ and live_prop02 and wheel126 in live_prop02
           and set(live_prop02) <= set(res02.get("identities_proposed") or ())
           and res02.get("identities_written") == [wheel126],
           f"rc={r02_.returncode} {out_of(r02_)[-300:]!r} res={res02} live map={live_prop02}")

    # T126-03: the override: a protruding-object clause that names its group is written for that group, by named_in_text,
    # with none of the default's links; the skill names the override. No code chooses the lens.
    skill126 = (REPO / "skills" / "run-pipeline_SKILL.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    r03_, fig03_, res03 = t126_add(code126, T126_PROTRUDE, "--identity", blind126, "--lens-basis", "named_in_text",
                                   "--lens-basis-text", "blind or have low vision")
    links03, _ = t126_links(fig03_) if fig03_ else (None, "")
    record("T126-03", "a protruding-object clause naming people who are blind or have low vision is written for that group by "
           "named_in_text with no default link, and the skill's guidance names the override",
           r03_.returncode == 0 and links03 == [(blind126, None, None, "named_in_text", "blind or have low vision", None)]
           and "protruding" in skill126 and "Overridden where the clause names another group" in skill126,
           f"rc={r03_.returncode} {out_of(r03_)[-250:]!r} links={links03}")

    # T126-04: context below tier 4 is refused, naming the sixteenth set; nothing is written.
    nf4, nl4 = n_figures(), n_links_now()
    r04_, fig04_, _ = t126_add(grey126, T126_CLAUSE, "--icf", reach126, *CTX("mounted at a height"))
    record("T126-04", "basis context on a source below tier 4 is refused naming the sixteenth set, and writes nothing",
           r04_.returncode != 0 and "sixteenth set" in out_of(r04_) and n_figures() == nf4 and n_links_now() == nl4,
           f"rc={r04_.returncode} {out_of(r04_)[-250:]!r}")

    # T126-05: context with a blank or missing reason is refused; a reason beside another basis is refused.
    def ll126(*extra):
        return run_cli("add-lens-link", "--extraction-id", str(fig126 or 0), "--icf", clear126, *extra, "--session", S)
    nl5 = n_links_now()
    refused5 = {
        "context, no reason": ll126("--basis", "context", "--basis-text", "mounted at a height"),
        "context, blank reason": ll126("--basis", "context", "--basis-text", "mounted at a height", "--basis-reason", "  "),
        "context, reason with no letter": ll126("--basis", "context", "--basis-text", "mounted at a height",
                                                "--basis-reason", "1200"),
        "named_in_text with a reason": ll126("--basis", "named_in_text", "--basis-text", "mounted at a height",
                                             "--basis-reason", T126_REASON),
        "heading with a reason": ll126("--basis", "heading", "--basis-text", "Section 3.8", "--basis-reason", T126_REASON),
        "study_participants with a reason": ll126("--basis", "study_participants", "--basis-text", "participants",
                                                  "--basis-reason", T126_REASON),
    }
    missed5 = [k for k, v in refused5.items() if v.returncode == 0]
    record("T126-05", "context with a missing, blank or letterless reason is refused, and a reason beside any other basis is "
           "refused; nothing is written",
           not missed5 and n_links_now() == nl5
           and "--basis-reason" in out_of(refused5["context, no reason"])
           and "belongs to basis `context` only" in out_of(refused5["named_in_text with a reason"]),
           f"not refused: {missed5}; {[out_of(v)[-120:] for v in refused5.values()]}")

    # T126-06: the context's words must be in the clause, its heading or a file saved for ITS source.
    r06a = ll126("--basis", "context", "--basis-text", "zq not anywhere xq", "--basis-reason", T126_REASON)
    r06b = ll126("--basis", "context", "--basis-text", "saved only for another source", "--basis-reason", T126_REASON)
    r06c = ll126("--basis", "context", "--basis-text", "applies to sanitary rooms", "--basis-reason", T126_REASON)
    r06d = run_cli("add-lens-link", "--extraction-id", str(fig126 or 0), "--needs",
                   t126_first("SELECT need_code FROM access_needs WHERE need_code<>? ORDER BY need_code", need126),
                   "--basis", "context", "--basis-text", "Section 3.8", "--basis-reason", T126_REASON, "--session", S)
    record("T126-06", "context words found nowhere, or only in a file saved for another source, are refused naming where it "
           "looked; words in the source's own saved scope clause and in its heading are accepted",
           r06a.returncode != 0 and r06b.returncode != 0 and "source_section" in out_of(r06b)
           and r06c.returncode == 0 and r06d.returncode == 0,
           f"{out_of(r06a)[-120:]!r} | {out_of(r06b)[-160:]!r} | {out_of(r06c)[-160:]!r} | {out_of(r06d)[-160:]!r}")

    # T126-07: a code row with no lens flag at all is refused (D-0182), as before.
    nf7, nl7 = n_figures(), n_links_now()
    r07_, _, _ = t126_add(code126, T126_CLAUSE + " (no lens)", *CTX("mounted at a height"))
    record("T126-07", "a code row with no lens flag is refused in the D-0182 words and writes nothing",
           r07_.returncode != 0 and "at least one lens" in out_of(r07_) and n_figures() == nf7 and n_links_now() == nl7,
           f"rc={r07_.returncode} {out_of(r07_)[-200:]!r}")

    # T126-08: a stored code figure holding only carried links takes a context link, then its carried link is retired
    # (the T-127 sequence). The probe is derived: the first such figure on the copy with a claim text to quote.
    probe8 = q("SELECT x.extraction_id, x.claim_text, MIN(k.link_id) FROM source_value_extractions x JOIN evidence_sources e "
               "ON e.ref_id = x.ref_id JOIN v_live_lens_links k ON k.extraction_id = x.extraction_id WHERE e.tier >= 4 "
               "AND TRIM(COALESCE(x.claim_text,'')) <> '' GROUP BY x.extraction_id HAVING SUM(k.basis <> 'carried') = 0 "

r=cli(*base,"--claim-text","TASK-PROBE Edge protection shall be provided for wheelchair users on each side of ramp runs","--identity","ALL","--identity","MOB","--icf","d465","--lens-basis","context","--lens-basis-text","wheelchair users","--lens-basis-reason","because")

import subprocess, sys, re, time, pathlib
T=sys.argv[1]; co=pathlib.Path(T)/"co"
dbp=co/"scripts/db.py"; aud=co/"scripts/audit/code_value_identity_audit.py"
D=dbp.read_text(); A=aud.read_text()
M=[
 ("M1 reason beside other basis allowed", dbp, 'if basis != "context" and reason is not None:', 'if False:'),
 ("M2 tier rule removed", dbp, 'if not (tier and tier[0] is not None and int(tier[0]) >= 4):\n            raise Refusal(\n                f"{context}: basis `context` is for', 'if False:\n            raise Refusal(\n                f"{context}: basis `context` is for'),
 ("M3 letter test removed (blank still refused)", dbp, 'if not reason or not re.search(r"[^\\W\\d_]", reason):', 'if not reason:'),
 ("M4 context words never looked for", dbp, 'found = (_as_whole_words(text, claim_text) or _as_whole_words(text, source_section)\n                 or _saved_text_has(text, ref_id))', 'found = True'),
 ("M4b context: saved-file search unscoped dropped (claim/section only)", dbp, 'found = (_as_whole_words(text, claim_text) or _as_whole_words(text, source_section)\n                 or _saved_text_has(text, ref_id))', 'found = (_as_whole_words(text, claim_text) or _as_whole_words(text, source_section))'),
 ("M5 retired map rows propose", dbp, 'f"WHERE m.retired_at IS NULL "', 'f"WHERE 1 "'),
 ("M6 need route (access_need_icf b/d) dropped from proposals", dbp, 'f"  AND (m.icf_code IN ({im}) OR m.icf_code IN (SELECT icf_code FROM access_need_icf "\n        f"       WHERE need_code IN ({nm}) AND icf_type <> \'e\')) "', 'f"  AND (m.icf_code IN ({im}) OR m.icf_code IN (SELECT icf_code FROM access_need_icf "\n        f"       WHERE need_code IN ({nm}) AND 0)) "'),
 ("M6b need route includes e-codes", dbp, 'f"       WHERE need_code IN ({nm}) AND icf_type <> \'e\')) "', 'f"       WHERE need_code IN ({nm}))) "'),
 ("M7 warning ignores tier", dbp, 'if not (tier and tier[0] is not None and int(tier[0]) >= 4) or live["identity_code"] \\', 'if live["identity_code"] \\'),
 ("M8 warning even when an identity is live", dbp, 'int(tier[0]) >= 4) or live["identity_code"] \\', 'int(tier[0]) >= 4) \\'),
 ("M9 parent never shown", dbp, 'parent = code[:-1] if len(code) > 4 and code[:-1] in titles else None', 'parent = None'),
 ("M10 need registry text not printed", dbp, 'out.append(f"  need {n}: design_obligation: {obligation}; absorbs: {absorbs}")', 'pass'),
 ("M11 add-lens-link proposals ignore the figure's live codes", dbp, 'conn, live["icf_code"] + ([code] if col == "icf_code" else []),\n            live["needs_code"] + ([code] if col == "needs_code" else []), "add-lens-link")', 'conn, ([code] if col == "icf_code" else []),\n            ([code] if col == "needs_code" else []), "add-lens-link")'),
 ("M12 add-lens-link never warns", dbp, '        _warn_identity_omitted(conn, extraction_id, fig["ref_id"])\n', ''),
 ("M13 add-lens-link identities_written always []", dbp, '"identities_proposed": proposed,\n                "identities_written": _live_lens_codes(conn, extraction_id)["identity_code"],\n                "dry_run": dry_run}', '"identities_proposed": [],\n                "identities_written": [],\n                "dry_run": dry_run}'),
 ("M14 derive-extraction drops the reason", dbp, '"lens_basis_text": lens_basis_text, "lens_basis_reason": lens_basis_reason,\n', '"lens_basis_text": lens_basis_text,\n'),
 ("M15 audit: tier filter removed", aud, 'WHERE e.tier >= 4 ORDER BY', 'WHERE 1 ORDER BY'),
 ("M16 audit: heading exclusion removed", aud, ' and any(r[3] != "heading" for r in links)', ''),
 ("M17 audit: list (ii) always none", aud, "{', '.join(unproposed) or 'none'}", "{'none'}"),
 ("M18 audit: list (ii) ignores retired map rows", aud, '(SELECT identity_code FROM identity_icf_map WHERE retired_at IS NULL)', '(SELECT identity_code FROM identity_icf_map)'),
 ("M19 audit: exit always 0", aud, 'return 1 if omitted else 0', 'return 0'),
 ("M20 audit: (iii) ignores need-row date", aud, 'for t in (p["map_created_at"], p["need_row_created_at"]))', 'for t in (p["map_created_at"],))'),
 ("M21 audit: (i) requires no proposal", aud, 'and props and any', 'and any'),
 ("M22 add-extraction proposals hidden (returns [] codes still)", dbp, '    print("\\n".join(out), file=sys.stderr)\n    return sorted({p["identity_code"] for p in props})', '    return sorted({p["identity_code"] for p in props})'),
]
only=sys.argv[2:] 
for name,path,old,new in M:
    if only and name.split()[0] not in only: continue
    src=path.read_text()
    if src.count(old)!=1:
        print(f"{name}: NEEDLE COUNT {src.count(old)} -- skipped", flush=True); continue
    path.write_text(src.replace(old,new))
    t=time.time()
    try:
        r=subprocess.run([sys.executable,"scripts/tests/test_db_amend_writers.py"],cwd=co,capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=900)
        out=r.stdout+r.stderr
        red=sorted(set(re.findall(r"\[✗\] (T\d+-\d+\w*)",out)))
        allred=re.findall(r"\[[^✓\]]\] (\S+?):",out)
        res=re.findall(r"RESULTS: .*",out)
        print(f"{name}: rc={r.returncode} red={allred or red} {res[-1:] or out[-200:]} [{time.time()-t:.0f}s]", flush=True)
    finally:
        path.write_text(src)
assert dbp.read_text()==D and aud.read_text()==A
print("restored")
PY

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
scripts/research/emit_batch_sql.py — capture a research batch out of a scratch DB.

DR-2026-08-19 §12.0 (F3). The research write path is a session-scoped scratch
copy of the database: `db.py` writes to it under GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH, so every
write-time refusal stays live (R9 duplicate-DOI lookups, H05/H07, CHECK
constraints, real exec_id allocation) instead of being reimplemented against a
renderer. This tool then extracts the delta as SQL, which feeds the ordinary
`emit_data_migration.py --input` and its ENUM/RANGE guards.

    python3 scripts/research/emit_batch_sql.py --scratch batch01.db --out batch01.sql

Both databases are opened read-only. This tool never writes to either one; the
only canonical write in a research session remains `migrate_db.py`.

The walk is additive by design. A row present in canonical but absent from the
scratch is REFUSED rather than rendered as a DELETE: a research batch adds
evidence, and a missing row means the scratch drifted from the canonical base
(usually a stale copy), which is a mistake to surface, not to replay.

ONE NARROW EXCEPTION, opt-in (2026-09-26). Some db.py writers delete on purpose, and an
additive-only capture made such a write impossible to ship (`unlink-admission` was the
first; since T-050 it retires the edge in place and deletes nothing, so it is captured as
an UPDATE and `--allow-delete search_admissions` refuses). `--allow-delete TABLE` renders
the missing rows of TABLE as DELETEs, and only when a writer in scripts/ actually
deletes from TABLE (dbcore.deletable_tables, derived from the writers the way the
capture set is). Every other missing row is still refused, so a stale copy is still
caught, and a deletion never happens unless the operator names the table.
"""

import argparse
import atexit
import os
import shutil
import sqlite3
import sys
import tempfile
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

# The canonical DB honours GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH like every other live script
# (scripts/audit/db_path_env_audit.py enforces this). The runbook invokes this
# tool without the variable set -- the scratch is named explicitly by --scratch --
# so the default resolves to data/guidebook.db in normal use.
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))
import dbcore                                                      # noqa: E402

DEFAULT_CANONICAL = os.environ.get("GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH", "data/guidebook.db")

# FK order: a parent is always emitted before anything that references it, so
# the migration applies cleanly even with foreign_keys enforcement on.
# TABLES MOVED TO scripts/dbcore.py 2026-08-25 and is imported below.
#
# WHY: this list and db.py's write coverage were two separate homes of one fact --
# "which tables a session may write" -- and that is exactly how a table became
# writable-but-invisible to capture. A rescue wrote 8 source_locators rows and this
# tool emitted 32 statements instead of 40, losing them with NO ERROR RAISED.
#
# THAT FIX WAS THE WRONG SHAPE, corrected 2026-09-13. One constant with two importers
